phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: More than 3 dots in the email local part.
trigger: More than 3 period characters in the email local part (before @).
explanation: Fraud farms often insert extra dots in Gmail-style addresses to create many unique-looking emails from one inbox or to evade naive duplicate checks. Legitimate users rarely use more than three dots in a username.
investigation: Compare with affiliate source and other email pattern flags. Multiple structure flags on one account increases confidence of templated signup.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email local part ends with 4–5 consecutive digits.
trigger: Local part ends with exactly 4 or 5 consecutive digits.
explanation: Bulk-generated accounts frequently append numeric suffixes to reuse a name stem across thousands of registrations.
investigation: Look for SEQUENTIAL_EMAIL or NAME_NUMBER_PATTERN on the same affiliate; check IP velocity and shared IP.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email appears randomly generated (low vowel ratio, odd consonant runs).
trigger: Heuristic detects low vowel ratio and random-looking consonant clusters in the local part.
explanation: Automatically generated strings often lack natural language letter patterns. This catches machine-created inboxes that are not obviously name-based.
investigation: High value combined with fast email validation or POV timing. Review profile images via CONTENT_REVIEW when present.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Templated name+number local part (e.g. firstname12lastname4567@domain).
trigger: Local part matches firstname+number+lastname+number style templates.
explanation: One of the highest-yield automated rules: fraud operations use predictable name-and-number email templates across campaigns.
investigation: Prioritize for manual review; often appears in clusters from the same affiliate. Pair with sequential email detection.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Written numbers in the email local part (one, two, three, etc.).
trigger: Local part contains English written numbers (e.g. one, two, three).
explanation: Some generators embed spelled-out numbers to vary addresses while keeping a scriptable pattern.
investigation: Usually secondary signal; escalate when combined with other email flags.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Word in local part appears in many emails in the current analysis batch.
trigger: A word from the local part appears in more than 3 emails in the current analysis batch (config: repeated_word_threshold).
explanation: Batch-level frequency detection finds shared tokens across many signups in the same run—common when a script reuses vocabulary.
investigation: Inspect the repeated word in details; drill into affiliate and time window for the batch.
score_points: 25 pts — Word frequency > threshold in batch [repeated_word_pattern]

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Local part matches configured fraud-associated names list.
trigger: Local part contains a name from the configured suspicious_names list (default includes fatima, muhammed).
explanation: Names that recur disproportionately in confirmed fraud are flagged for review. List is editable in config.
investigation: Validate against recent confirmed fraud outcomes; propose list updates monthly.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Predicted gender from email/name does not match declared gender (user1).
trigger: Gender inferred from email/name (gender-guesser) conflicts with declared gender (user1/custom_u1), high-confidence only.
explanation: Declares one gender but uses an email local part strongly associated with another—common in misrepresented or scripted profiles.
investigation: Androgynous or unknown names are skipped. Confirm declared gender and billing name on paid accounts.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Paid records only: billing first name gender ≠ declared gender (high-confidence mismatches only).
trigger: Paid records: billing first name gender ≠ declared gender (high-confidence only).
explanation: Payment name inconsistent with profile gender is a strong paid-fraud indicator—often chargeback or stolen-card scenarios.
investigation: Cross-check shared_card flags and card type. Confirm with processor billing data.
score_points: 35 pts — Paid data with high-confidence mismatch [billing_gender_mismatch]

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email matches a theme bucket: REAL_ESTATE, CONSTRUCTION, CRYPTO, or FINANCE.
trigger: Local part contains keywords for real estate, construction, crypto, or finance themes.
explanation: Theme clustering groups niche keyword spam that appears in coordinated fraud waves (investment/crypto scams, etc.). Stored flag: THEME_CLUSTER_<THEME>.
investigation: Review campaign and affiliate; themes often spike together in time.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email verified within 20 seconds (CSV POV fields).
trigger: CSV POV fields: email verified within 20 seconds of signup.
explanation: Human users rarely complete verification instantly; sub-20s timing suggests automation or pre-validated inboxes.
investigation: Treat as critical if Admin email_validated timing confirms. Highest priority queue.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email verified within 40 seconds (CSV POV fields).
trigger: CSV POV: verified within 21–40 seconds.
explanation: Still abnormally fast for organic signup; slightly lower weight than 20s tier.
investigation: Compare with Admin validation timestamps when available.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Email verified within 60 seconds (CSV POV fields).
trigger: CSV POV: verified within 41–60 seconds.
explanation: Fast validation band; meaningful when combined with other fraud signals.
investigation: Use as supporting signal unless affiliate shows widespread fast POV.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Email validated within 60s (+50) or 61–120s (+30) of account creation (Admin API).
trigger: Admin API: seconds from account creation to email validation ≤ 60 or ≤ 120.
explanation: Strongest automated signal when platform timestamps are available—mirrors manual POV analysis at scale.
investigation: Prioritize ≤60s accounts for affiliate termination discussions. Flag stored as email_validated_{N}s(+points).
score_points: 50 pts — Validation ≤ 60s after registration [email_validated_60s] | 30 pts — Validation 61–120s [email_validated_120s]
notes: Also uses email_validated_120s config for 61–120 second window. | Stored as: email_validated_{N}s(+pts)

phase_description: Second pass on the analysis batch; only matching accounts are flagged.
summary: Same affiliate: same text stem + domain with 4+ distinct numeric suffixes on local part.
trigger: Same affiliate: same letter stem (≥4 chars) + same domain, with 4+ distinct numeric suffixes on local part.
explanation: Detects factory-style email generation (e.g. maucheesee71@, maucheesee76@) without requiring consecutive numbers.
investigation: Affiliate-level abuse indicator—review entire affiliate cohort sharing the stem.

phase_description: Second pass on the analysis batch; only matching accounts are flagged.
summary: Affiliate has abnormally high WOMAN registration share (default ≥15%); flags WOMAN accounts from that affiliate.
trigger: Affiliate WOMAN share ≥ ~15% (configurable in build_gender_concentration_map) with sufficient sample; baseline ~0.9%.
explanation: Flags only WOMAN registrations from affiliates with abnormal gender mix—often mislabeled or scripted female profiles.
investigation: Affiliate quality conversation; compare to campaign and geo. Only flagged gender rows receive points.
score_points: 25 pts — WOMAN account from concentrated affiliate [woman_concentration]

phase_description: Second pass on the analysis batch; only matching accounts are flagged.
summary: Non-excluded domain (default: not gmail.com) is ≥5% of affiliate emails with ≥20 registrations; flags accounts on that domain only.
trigger: Affiliate has ≥20 emails in batch; non-excluded domain (default: not gmail.com) is ≥5% of that affiliate's domains.
explanation: Fraud sources funnel traffic through disposable or niche domains. Gmail is excluded by default because it dominates legitimate traffic.
investigation: Inspect domain WHOIS/reputation; only accounts on the concentrated domain are flagged—not all affiliate traffic.
score_points: 20 pts — Email domain matches concentrated pair (affiliate, domain) [affiliate_domain_concentration]

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Registration IP has 10+ signups in one hour (within analysis batch).
trigger: Registration IP has 10+ signups within one hour in the analysis batch (config: ip_velocity_threshold).
explanation: Classic fraud-ring signal—single IP driving volume in a short window.
investigation: Check SHARED_IP flags and datacenter/VPN ASN. Consider IP block at affiliate level.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Registration IP has 5+ signups in one hour (within analysis batch).
trigger: Registration IP has 5–9 signups within one hour in batch.
explanation: Elevated velocity; weaker alone but useful in combination.
investigation: Trend IP over multiple days if data available.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Same registration IP used by 10+ accounts in batch.
trigger: Same registration IP appears on 10+ accounts in the batch.
explanation: Shared infrastructure—café, VPN, or fraud farm.
investigation: Distinguish datacenter vs residential via enrichment flags.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Same registration IP used by 3–9 accounts in batch.
trigger: Same registration IP on 3–9 accounts in batch.
explanation: Moderate sharing; may be legitimate NAT but worth review on high-payout affiliates.
investigation: Correlate with email patterns.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: Desktop signup device; 20 pts Windows 10, 10 pts other desktops.
trigger: Signup user-agent indicates desktop; Windows 10 vs other desktop OS tiers.
explanation: Fraud farms often use Windows 10 desktops at scale; other desktops scored lower.
investigation: Combine with IP and email signals—desktop alone is weak.
score_points: 20 pts — Windows 10 desktop [desktop_windows_10] | 10 pts — Other desktop OS [desktop_other]
notes: Other desktop uses desktop_other config key.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: 3+ accounts from the same US state in batch.
trigger: 3+ accounts in batch share the same US state (geo from data).
explanation: Geographic clustering can indicate targeted fraud or proxy concentration.
investigation: Compare to affiliate's expected geo; check city-level cluster flag.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: 3+ accounts from the same US city and state in batch.
trigger: 3+ accounts share same US city and state.
explanation: Tighter cluster than state-only—higher confidence of coordinated signups.
investigation: Map to IP clusters and registration times.

phase_description: Applied to each row during lead/email analysis.
summary: 3+ accounts from the same international city in batch.
trigger: 3+ accounts share same non-US city.
explanation: International city clustering—common in outsourced fraud operations.
investigation: Check login_high_risk_country and geo_login_mismatch.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Registration IP country ≠ login IP country.
trigger: GeoIP country of registration IP ≠ GeoIP country of login IP.
explanation: Cross-country movement between signup and login is suspicious on dating products when paired with other signals. Different from raw IP string mismatch.
investigation: Confirm countries in flag text. High-risk login country adds separate points.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Same country but registration state ≠ login state.
trigger: Same country but US state (or region) differs between registration and login IP.
explanation: Cross-state moves happen legitimately but add risk when combined with automation signals.
investigation: Not scored for different cities within same state.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Login IP in configured high-risk country list.
trigger: Login IP country in config high_risk_countries (default: NG, GH, CI, CM, PH, RO, MD, ID).
explanation: Login from geographies over-represented in dating fraud ops.
investigation: Validate against declared geo in CSV; list is configurable.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Login IP country ≠ geo_country from leads CSV.
trigger: Login IP country ≠ geo_country from affiliate/leads CSV.
explanation: Cross-source inconsistency—lead data says one country, login IP another.
investigation: Data quality vs fraud—check if CSV geo is stale or VPN-related.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Registration IP resolves to datacenter/cloud hosting ASN.
trigger: Registration IP ASN classified as datacenter/cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure, etc.).
explanation: Consumer dating signups rarely originate from cloud host IPs.
investigation: ASN name appears in flag. Pair with email automation flags.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Login IP resolves to datacenter/cloud hosting ASN.
trigger: Login IP ASN is datacenter/cloud.
explanation: Bots and scripted logins often use hosted infrastructure.
investigation: Compare to registration IP type.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Registration IP on known VPN/proxy ASN.
trigger: Registration IP ASN matches known VPN/proxy providers.
explanation: Anonymized registration path—elevated risk on affiliate traffic.
investigation: VPN at registration + fast validation is high priority.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Login IP on known VPN/proxy ASN.
trigger: Login IP on VPN/proxy ASN.
explanation: Common for fraud operators masking location.
investigation: Compare with geo_login_mismatch.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Same non-excluded card linked to 3+ other accounts (35 pts) or 5+ (50 pts). Major issuers excluded.
trigger: Confirmed shared card (Used By, not fuzzy match) links account to 3+ or 5+ other DUIDs; major issuers excluded.
explanation: Same payment credential across many accounts indicates fraud ring or stolen card testing.
investigation: Use Admin shared cards view; 5+ is ring-level priority. QA cards/DUIDs can be whitelisted in config.
score_points: 35 pts — 3–4 other accounts on same card [shared_card_3plus] | 50 pts — 5+ other accounts [shared_card_5plus]
notes: 5+ accounts uses shared_card_5plus config. | Stored as: shared_card_{N}_accounts(+pts)

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: American Express on file (rare baseline on dating sites).
trigger: Any Amex cardType on account payment methods.
explanation: Amex has near-zero baseline on typical dating traffic—any appearance is anomalous.
investigation: Verify charge outcomes; check billing gender mismatch.

phase_description: After Admin API + GeoIP enrichment (typically paid/enriched accounts).
summary: Business/corporate card description on a dating site account.
trigger: cardDescription contains business/corporate/commercial/company/enterprise keywords.
explanation: Business cards are inherently unusual for consumer dating purchases.
investigation: Confirm description text in Admin; no issuer exclusions.

phase_description: Batch rule after enrichment completes (e.g. Discover concentration).
summary: Affiliate enriched accounts: Discover cards exceed threshold (default >10%, min 10 accounts); flags Discover-card accounts only.
trigger: Post-enrichment: affiliate has >10% Discover cards among enriched accounts (default), minimum 10 enriched accounts.
explanation: Discover baseline ~2% site-wide; affiliate-level spikes suggest bad traffic mix.
investigation: Only Discover-card accounts flagged. Affiliate negotiation / cap traffic.
score_points: 20 pts — Discover account from hot affiliate [discover_concentration]

phase_description: Review workflow; may not add risk points.
summary: Profile photo present and (upload <180s after registration OR suspicious email/identity flags) — content/image review queue.
trigger: Profile image uploaded AND (upload <180s after registration OR suspicious email/identity flags).
explanation: Queues accounts for manual image review (stock, stolen, AI faces)—not always a score driver (default 0 points).
investigation: Reverse image search; compare upload timing. Does not replace email/card investigation.

phase_description: Data issue, not a fraud pattern.
summary: Missing email on record; fraud analysis skipped for row.
trigger: Email field empty or missing on input row.
explanation: Row skipped for pattern analysis; indicates export or pipeline data gap.
investigation: Fix upstream data—not a fraud finding.
